Hello! As a debugging agent and expert, I've analyzed the build failure. Here is my assessment and the recommended solution.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library. The error message is:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

This error occurs because the `CMakeLists.txt` provided by METIS is not compatible with the standard out-of-source build pattern used in your Dockerfile (where a `build` directory is created inside the source directory). The CMake script incorrectly tries to find a source subdirectory named `build`, which clashes with the name of the directory being used for the build output.

### Recommended Fix

The most robust solution is to bypass the problematic CMake configuration for METIS and use its native, well-documented `make`-based build system instead. This involves replacing the sequence of `cmake` commands for METIS with the appropriate `make` commands. This change is scoped only to the METIS build section and resolves the issue directly.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# Provides a modern, stable base with a rich package repository.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for some build systems, kept for general utility.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # FIX: Switched to the native Makefile build system as the CMake configuration
    # is incompatible with the out-of-source build pattern.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    make config prefix=/usr/local shared=1 && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it
    # This preserves the 'data' directory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # FIX: Switched from 'make config' to 'cmake' for a more robust build process,
    # resolving the 'GKlib.h: No such file or directory' compilation error.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake .. -DSHARED=1 -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it
    # FIX: Changed 'cp -r data/*' to 'cp -r data' to preserve the 'data' directory
    # structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

Hello, I am the debugging agent. I have analyzed the Dockerfile and the associated error log to identify the problem.

### Problem Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library, which is a dependency for the Laghos application. The error message from CMake indicates it cannot find a required subdirectory:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

### Root Cause Analysis

The `xinclude` directory is a git submodule within the METIS repository. The Dockerfile attempts to clone the repository and its submodules using `git clone --recursive`. However, this command can sometimes fail to properly initialize all submodules, especially when combined with a shallow clone (`--depth 1`).

When CMake runs, it doesn't find the submodule's source code. The METIS `CMakeLists.txt` has a fallback to clone the missing dependency, but this process is also failing within the build environment, leading to the error.

The most reliable method to ensure git submodules are correctly initialized in a script is to perform the actions in separate, explicit steps. I will modify the Dockerfile to:
1.  Clone the main METIS repository without the `--recursive` flag.
2.  Add a new command, `git submodule update --init`, to explicitly fetch and initialize the required submodules.

This small change makes the build process more robust and directly resolves the submodule issue. The rest of the Dockerfile is correct and already fulfills the other requirements.

ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \

    make -j${NPROCS} && \

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library. The specific error is:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

This indicates that the CMake build system for METIS is unable to locate one of its required subdirectories (`xinclude`, a git submodule). The issue stems from the way CMake is being invoked. While `cmake . -B build` is a valid modern syntax for an out-of-source build, the METIS `CMakeLists.txt` file appears to have trouble with relative paths when invoked this way from within the source directory.

The most robust and conventional way to perform an out-of-source CMake build is to create a separate build directory, change into it, and then invoke `cmake` pointing back to the parent source directory. This avoids any path ambiguity.

# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.

    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,

ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # FIX: Renamed the temporary build directory to 'build-cmake' to avoid a name
    # collision with a source directory named 'build', resolving the CMake error.

    make -j${NPROCS} && \

### Problem Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library, which is a dependency for the Laghos application. The error message from CMake indicates it cannot find a required subdirectory:

CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.

The `xinclude` directory is a git submodule within the METIS repository. The Dockerfile attempts to clone the repository and its submodules using `git clone --recursive`. However, this command can sometimes fail to properly initialize all submodules, especially when combined with a shallow clone (`--depth 1`).

1.  Clone the main METIS repository without the `--recursive` flag.
2.  Add a new command, `git submodule update --init`, to explicitly fetch and initialize the required submodules.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library. The error message is:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

This error occurs because the `CMakeLists.txt` provided by METIS is not compatible with the standard out-of-source build pattern used in your Dockerfile (where a `build` directory is created inside the source directory). The CMake script incorrectly tries to find a source subdirectory named `build`, which clashes with the name of the directory being used for the build output.

The most robust solution is to bypass the problematic CMake configuration for METIS and use its native, well-documented `make`-based build system instead. ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \

    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)

    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \

2.  `cd` into that `build` directory.
3.  Run `cmake ..` to configure the build.
4.  Run `cmake --build .` and `cmake --install .` to compile and install from within the build directory.

# Provides a modern, stable base with a rich package repository.

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for building METIS.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.

    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,

ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp

ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

    make -j${NPROCS} && \

    cd ../.. && \

    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \

         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \

         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory

    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \

    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.

    \

CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Cloning the latest branch and using a modern, in-source CMake build.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    cmake . -B build \
          -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -DSHARED=ON \
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    cmake --build build -j ${NPROCS} && \
    cmake --install build && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it.
    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# Provides a modern, stable base with a rich package repository.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for some build systems, kept for general utility.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # FIX: Use --recursive to clone the GKlib submodule required by METIS.
    # This resolves the 'GKlib.h: No such file or directory' compilation error.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    make config prefix=/usr/local shared=1 && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.

    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \

    \

    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size

# Set the final working directory for the container

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library, which is the first dependency being built. The specific error from the log is:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

This indicates that the `cmake` configuration command is failing. The command being used, `cmake . -B build`, attempts an "out-of-source" build by creating the build files inside a `build` subdirectory. However, for this specific version or configuration of the METIS `CMakeLists.txt`, this modern syntax appears to be causing an issue with relative path resolution, leading it to incorrectly look for a source directory inside the build directory.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this, we will modify the METIS build process to use a more traditional and universally compatible out-of-source build pattern. This involves manually creating the `build` directory, changing into it, and then invoking `cmake` to configure the project from there. This approach is more robust and avoids the path confusion that is causing the build to fail.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile with the necessary changes applied to the METIS build section.

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
# Provides a modern, stable base with a rich package repository.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for building METIS.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Cloning the latest branch and using a modern, in-source CMake build.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake .. \
          -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -DSHARED=ON \
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it.
    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for some build systems, kept for general utility.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # FIX: Switched to the native Makefile build system as the CMake build is problematic
    # in v5.2.1 and causes a 'subdirectory does not exist' error.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v5.2.1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    make config prefix=/usr/local shared=1 && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it
    # This preserves the 'data' directory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Cloning the latest branch and using a modern, in-source CMake build.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    cmake . -B build \
          -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -DSHARED=ON \
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    cmake --build build -j ${NPROCS} && \
    cmake --install build && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)

    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)

         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \

         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory

# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.

    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \

    mkdir /app && \

    \

# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,

CMD ["/bin/bash"]

    \

# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.

    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local

# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it
    # This preserves the 'data' directory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

When CMake runs, it doesn't find the submodule's source code. The METIS `CMakeLists.txt` has a fallback to clone the missing dependency, but this process is also failing within the build environment, leading to the error.

### Recommended Solution

The most reliable method to ensure git submodules are correctly initialized in a script is to perform the actions in separate, explicit steps. I will modify the Dockerfile to:
1.  Clone the main METIS repository without the `--recursive` flag.
2.  Add a new command, `git submodule update --init`, to explicitly fetch and initialize the required submodules.

This small change makes the build process more robust and directly resolves the submodule issue. The rest of the Dockerfile is correct and already fulfills the other requirements.

# Provides a modern, stable base with a rich package repository.

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for building METIS.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.

    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Pinned to a stable version and using a standard out-of-source CMake build.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v5.2.1 https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    git submodule update --init && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake .. \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
        -DSHARED=ON \
        -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it.
    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Prevent interactive dialogues during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install core dependencies for building C++/MPI applications
# - build-essential: Includes g++, make, and other compilation tools.
# - git: For cloning source code repositories.
# - cmake: Required for building METIS.
# - wget: Utility for downloading files.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: OpenMPI runtime and development libraries.
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    cmake \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Cloning the latest branch and using a modern, in-source CMake build.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    cmake . -B build \
          -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -DSHARED=ON \
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    cmake --build build -j ${NPROCS} && \
    cmake --install build && \
    cd .. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it.
    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the METIS library. The error message is:

```
CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:50 (add_subdirectory):
  add_subdirectory given source "build/xinclude" which is not an existing
  directory.
```

This error occurs because the `CMakeLists.txt` provided by METIS is not compatible with the standard out-of-source build pattern used in your Dockerfile (where a `build` directory is created inside the source directory). The CMake script incorrectly tries to find a source subdirectory named `build`, which clashes with the name of the directory being used for the build output.

The most robust solution is to bypass the problematic CMake configuration for METIS and use its native, well-documented `make`-based build system instead.     && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes.
# These settings improve compatibility and prevent errors in environments
# without specialized HPC hardware (like InfiniBand).
# - BTL/PML: Use TCP for communication, excluding hardware-specific transports.
# - OVERSUBSCRIBE: Allow more MPI processes than available CPU cores,
#   which is common in container orchestration.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_rmaps_base_oversubscribe=1

# --- Build and Install Dependencies ---
# This single RUN command builds and installs all required libraries (METIS, HYPRE, MFEM)
# from source. Building in a temporary directory and cleaning up reduces final image size.
# All libraries are installed to /usr/local to be easily found by subsequent steps.
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/var/cache/apt \
    export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export BUILD_DIR=/tmp/build && \
    mkdir -p ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    cd ${BUILD_DIR} && \
    \
    # 1. Build and install METIS (Graph Partitioning Library)
    # Using a classic out-of-source build to avoid CMake configuration issues.
    # The '-fcommon' flag is added for compatibility with modern GCC compilers.
    git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS.git && \
    cd METIS && \
    mkdir build && cd build && \
    cmake .. \
          -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr/local \
          -DSHARED=ON \
          -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-fcommon" && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 2. Build and install HYPRE (Linear Solvers)
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre.git && \
    cd hypre/src && \
    ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --enable-shared && \
    make -j${NPROCS} && \
    make install && \
    cd ../.. && \
    \
    # 3. Build and install MFEM (Finite Element Methods Library)
    # This build links against the previously installed METIS and HYPRE.
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j${NPROCS} \
         MFEM_USE_MPI=YES \
         MFEM_USE_METIS=YES \
         HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local \
         METIS_DIR=/usr/local && \
    make install prefix=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 4. Cleanup build directory
    rm -rf ${BUILD_DIR}

# --- Build Laghos Application ---
# This command clones the Laghos repository, builds the executable,
# copies the binary to the system PATH, and prepares the final application directory.
RUN export NPROCS=$(nproc) && \
    export LAGHOS_SRC=/tmp/laghos_src && \
    \
    # 1. Clone the Laghos source code (latest default branch)
    git clone https://github.com/LLNL/Laghos.git ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    cd ${LAGHOS_SRC} && \
    \
    # 2. Build the Laghos executable, linking against MFEM in /usr/local
    make -j${NPROCS} MFEM_DIR=/usr/local && \
    \
    # 3. Copy the compiled executable to a location on the system PATH
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    \
    # 4. Create the final application directory and copy the required data directory into it.
    # This preserves the 'data' subdirectory structure, which is expected by the application at runtime.
    mkdir /app && \
    cp -r data /app/ && \
    \
    # 5. Clean up the source code to reduce final image size
    rm -rf ${LAGHOS_SRC}

# Set the final working directory for the container
WORKDIR /app

# Default command: Start an interactive bash session.
# The user can override this to run the application, e.g.,
# docker run <image> mpirun -np 4 laghos -p 0 -m data/cube01_hex.mesh -rs 3 -tf 0.6
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

```
